after.title: Preprint: Digital Twin-Based Risk Stratification Integrating Aortic Shape and Wall Mechanics in Acute Uncomplicated Type B Aortic Dissection
after.authors: Liu, M.; Zhou, Z.; Du, Y.; Cebull, H. L.; Dong, H.; Oshinski, J. N.; Elefteriades, J. A.; Gleason, R. L.; Leshnower, B. G.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Emory University
after.abstract: Objective This study evaluated whether patient-specific digital twins integrating 3D aortic anatomy and structural wall stress could identify patients with acute uncomplicated type B aortic dissection (AUTBAD) at high risk for adverse aortic events. Methods We analyzed CTAs from 50 patients extracted from a 400 AUTBAD patient database treated with optimal medical therapy from 1999-2025. Digital twin models were constructed, and statistical shape modeling and reduced-order fluid-structure interaction analysis were performed. Anatomic shape and biomechanical stress data were integrated into models predicting freedom from aortic events, defined as intervention or aortic-related death, using leave-one-out cross-validation. A cross-validated risk score was generated for each patient, with higher scores indicating higher event risk. Results At diagnosis, the median descending aortic diameter was 40.61 mm. During follow-up, 35 patients experienced an aortic event: 28 interventions (56%) and 7 aortic-related deaths (14%). Stratification by descending aortic diameter above or below 40.61 mm yielded higher- versus lower-risk aortic event-free survival of 72.0% versus 84.0% at 1 year and 27.8% versus 56.7% at 6 years (p=0.035; C-index=0.590). In the cross-validated multidimensional model combining morphology and structural stress, higher- versus lower-risk event-free survival was 60.0% versus 96.0% at 1 year and 12.5% versus 68.9% at 6 years (p<0.001; C-index=0.792). Conclusions Digital twin modeling integrating morphology and wall stress provided greater risk separation than univariable predictors in AUTBAD patients. With independent validation, patient-specific AUTBAD risk stratification using geometric and biomechanical data may ultimately contribute to identification of high-risk patients who may benefit from early endovascular repair.

after.title: Preprint: Can dental EHR data support a learning health system? Completeness, consistency, and accuracy of structured versus narrative diagnoses
after.authors: Chuang, Y.-S.; Lin, G.-H.; Lee, C.-T.; Brandon, R.; Walji, M. F.; Jiang, X.; Tokede, B.
after.author_corresponding_institution: The University of Texas Health Science Center at Houston
after.abstract: Introduction Electronic health record (EHR) data increasingly drive quality monitoring and research, yet their reliability in dentistry is uncertain. We compared the completeness, consistency, and accuracy of periodontal diagnoses captured in two different formats (structured fields versus narrative notes) across two academic dental centers sharing the same EHR platform and diagnostic terminology. Methods In this retrospective study of qualifying periodontal encounters (2021), structured diagnoses were extracted by SQL and narrative diagnoses by a fine-tuned RoBERTa NLP model. A random sample (~20%) was independently reviewed by two board-certified periodontists, with disagreements resolved by consensus, to form the gold standard. Outcomes were completeness (presence of a diagnosis), consistency (agreement between formats), and accuracy (agreement with the gold standard), with ordinal periodontal stage compared using quadratic weighted {kappa}. Results Across 4,542 encounters, completeness varied widely by site and format (34.7% - 84.5%), and neither format was consistently more complete; at one site, over one-third of encounters (35.8%) had no documented diagnosis in either format. Among dual-documented encounters, agreement between formats was substantial but imperfect ({kappa} = 0.86 and 0.80). Accuracy against the gold standard was modest for both sources (all near 50%), with narrative notes numerically higher at both sites and favored by the severity-weighted {kappa}, though raw differences were not significant. Pooled across sites, the formats diverged in 14.8% of dual-documented encounters, 8.4% by two or more stages, with the structured field carrying the milder stage in 67.9% of disagreements. Conclusions Structured and unstructured periodontal diagnoses each matched expert adjudication only about half the time, and neither was consistently more complete. Narrative notes held a small severity-weighted accuracy advantage, and coded fields more often carried the milder stage when the two disagreed. These convergent, cross-site patterns appear systematic rather than site-specific and expose latent risks for analytics and decision support. Improving dental EHR data quality will require workflows that combine the computability of coded entries with the fidelity of free text.

after.author_corresponding_institution: University of Nebraska-Lincoln, Lincoln, NE, USA
after.abstract: Introduction: Dementia and late-life depression are rising rapidly in sub-Saharan Africa, yet prevention frameworks remain focused on individual behaviour. Multidimensional poverty is a plausible structural determinant of brain health but is rarely assessed. Methods: This cross-sectional analysis of the community-based Akili Mali study assessed adults aged 60 years and older in three rural communities in Kilimanjaro, Tanzania. Outcomes were the 15-item Geriatric Depression Scale (GDS-15), IDEA cognitive screen, CERAD ten-word list, and verbal fluency. Deprivation was measured with a nine-indicator Alkire-Foster Multidimensional Deprivation Index. Missing data were multiply imputed; models adjusted for age, sex, education, community, comorbidity, and health behaviours. Results: Of 1054 participants (mean age 70.2 years [SD 9.35]; 629 [59.7%] women), 840 (81.9%) of 1026 were multidimensionally deprived. Each unit increase in deprivation score predicted a higher GDS-15 score ({beta} 4.83, 95% CI 3.82 to 5.83), higher odds of screen-positive depression (odds ratio 17.18, 6.89 to 42.83), lower IDEA score ({beta} -1.97, -2.97 to -0.97), and lower verbal fluency ({beta} -2.57, -3.77 to -1.36; all p<0.001). CERAD measures and self-reported impairment showed no association. At community level this gradient inverted: the most deprived community had the lowest depression and highest cognition, yet perceived social standing did not differ. Conclusion: Multidimensional deprivation was near-universal and independently associated with worse brain health. The community-level inversion, with perceived social standing equivalent across communities of unequal material circumstances, indicates that absolute deprivation alone does not explain the distribution of brain health. Relative position and community resilience are priorities for study

after.authors: Eboga, H.; Lubaale, Y.; Oguttu, F.; Nantale, R.; Tsekpetse, P.; Makoko, B. T.; Kawala, E.; Mugahi, R.; Kazibwe, A.; Okia, D.; Musaba, M. W.; Kibuule, D.; Mukunya, D.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Department of Community and Public Health, Busitema University Faculty of Health Sciences, Mbale, Uganda
after.abstract: Background Uganda continues to experience a high burden of maternal and child morbidity and mortality, partly due to suboptimal utilization and quality of reproductive, maternal, newborn, and child health services. To address these challenges, the Ministry of Health of Uganda, with World Bank funding, implemented results-based financing (RBF) through the Uganda Reproductive, Maternal, and Child Health Services Improvement Project (URMCHIP) in selected districts. Although RBF has been implemented for nearly a decade, evidence on its impact on maternal and child health service indicators in Uganda remains limited. This study assessed the effect of RBF on selected maternal and child health indicators in Mayuge District, Uganda. Methods We retrospectively reviewed the records between July 2018 and June 2019 as the pre-intervention period, July 2019 to June 2021 as the intervention period, and July 2021 to June 2023 as the post-intervention period. We conducted multiple-group interrupted time-series analyses to compare trends in selected maternal and child health indicators between four intervention and three non-intervention health facilities. Results After the implementation of RBF, the number of births in the intervention facilities increased by 1.67 births per month (95% CI [0.19, 3.16]) as compared to the control facilities. The number of women receiving modern family planning methods in intervention facilities increased by 34.1 women per month (CI [25.8, 42.4] as compared to the control facilities. The number of children under five years seen at the outpatient department slightly decreased by -0.24 children per month (CI [-9.58, 9.10]). There was a decline in facility-based births and the number of clients receiving modern family planning methods following the discontinuation of results-based financing in the intervention health facilities. Conclusions There was an improvement in selected maternal and child health indicators in the intervention health facilities following the implementation of RBF, with a subsequent decline in facility-based births and the number of clients receiving modern family planning methods after RBF was discontinued. We recommend that policymakers consider allocating additional funds towards RBF to improve health service delivery.

after.authors: Rode, J.; Hutchinson, A. N.; Thunberg, P.; Brummer, R. J.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Orebro University
after.abstract: Background: Despite increasing interest in the gut-brain axis, the role of the autonomic nervous system and the brainstem in human gut-brain signalling remain largely unknown. Objective: To characterise resting state functional connectivity (FC) of the brainstem in healthy older adults and to examine its association with a variety of factors relevant to ageing and the gut-brain axis, and to assess if brainstem FC is altered by probiotic intervention. Design: Randomised, double-blinded, placebo-controlled trial in 60-80-year-olds (55 women/28 men) with six-weeks Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus HN001 intervention in a non-encapsulated and microencapsulated formulation. Brainstem-optimised functional magnetic resonance imaging was performed before and after intervention. Results: At baseline, age correlated positively with FC of locus coeruleus (LC) and dorsal raphe nucleus (DRN) with pre-/postcentral gyrus, as well as of periaqueductal gray (PAG) with temporal/supramarginal gyrus and planum temporale. FC of PAG with precuneus cortex and cingulate gyrus correlated with cognitive status and mood. Perceived stress correlated with FC between nucleus tractus solitarius and occipital cortex, angular/temporal gyrus. FC of DRN differed between men and women. All p<0.0063. Following probiotic intervention, a significant time*group interaction and main time effect were observed for FC of LC and ventral tegmental area. FC of both with occipital pole/cortex and cerebellum, and of LC with pre-/postcentral gyrus, superior parietal lobule, insular/opercular cortex, putamen, and planum polare showed within-group changes (non-encapsulated), no between-group differences were observed (all p<0.0056). Conclusion: Brainstem-to-cortex FC at rest correlates with several phenotypic characteristics implicated in healthy ageing and may be modifiable by probiotic supplementation.

after.title: Preprint: Transdiagnostic Functional Brain Alterations Across Familial and Phenotypic Risk Samples: A Meta-Analysis
after.authors: Millman, Z. B.; Burdinski, D.; Rodriguez, J.; Chatterjea, T.; Blackford, J. U.; Holt, D. J.; Clauss, J. A.
after.author_corresponding_institution: University of Iowa
after.abstract: Importance: Psychiatric risk factors are often associated with multiple clinical outcomes. However, it remains unclear whether functional brain activation changes are shared across risk for mood, anxiety, and psychotic disorders. Objective: To determine which patterns of functional brain activation are shared across risk for different psychiatric disorders, defined using phenotypic (e.g., clinical) and familial risk paradigms, relative to control samples. Data Sources: PubMed and Web of Science were searched for task-based functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) studies involving samples at risk for a mood, anxiety, or psychotic disorder, published between January 2000 and July 2026. Study Selection: Studies published in English, with whole brain results, comparing a high-risk sample to a control sample, with a mean age of 30 years or less, were included. Of the 5,748 studies screened, 101 met selection criteria. Data Extraction and Synthesis: Peak voxel coordinates from contrasts were extracted. Study quality was assessed using an adapted neuroimaging methods quality checklist. Peak coordinates were pooled within studies, and a random effects activation likelihood estimation meta-analysis was conducted using the Python package JALE. Main Outcomes and Measures: Statistical maps of spatial convergence in task-related brain activation were computed across risk groups and within subgroups defined by disorder risk (mood, anxiety, or psychotic disorder risk), ascertainment paradigm (phenotypic, familial), and task domain (cognitive, affective, reward). Statistical significance was assessed using permutation-based cluster-level family-wise error (cFWE) correction. Results: The studies included comprised 2534 high-risk participants and 2686 controls. Across psychosis, mood, and anxiety risk groups, there was a common area of functional activation in the left lateral prefrontal cortex (k = 319, p < 0.05 cFWE), reflecting greater activation in high-risk groups compared to controls. Approximately 30% of studies in each risk group contributed to this finding, reflecting both ascertainment paradigms and all three task types. Within the psychosis risk group, additional alterations were identified in the orbitofrontal cortex and anterior insula. Conclusions and Relevance: Increased left lateral prefrontal activation was shared across risk groups despite methodological heterogeneity. Because this region supports higher-order executive functioning and undergoes prolonged maturation, this finding may represent a shared marker of vulnerability across psychiatric risk groups.

after.title: Preprint: Disability-relevant demyelination in multiple sclerosis: five-year evolution following diagnosis
after.authors: York, E. N.; Meijboom, R.; Thrippleton, M. J.; Bastin, M.; Kampaite, A.; Martin, S.-J.; Kearns, P. K. A.; Hunt, D.; Chandran, S.; Waldman, A.; FutureMS Consortium,
after.author_corresponding_institution: University of Edinburgh
after.abstract: Improved understanding of how myelin damage contributes to disability in multiple sclerosis (MS) is needed to inform targeted therapeutic strategies and improve clinical trial platforms. Magnetization transfer saturation (MTsat) and T1 relaxometry provide in vivo quantitative MRI measures of myelin integrity, and may offer insights into disability-relevant pathology beyond inflammatory relapse. This longitudinal study explores the relationship between early demyelination and disability progression over the first five years following diagnosis. 62 people with relapsing-remitting (pwRR)MS ([≤] 6 months post-diagnosis, 48 female, mean age 38 years) underwent baseline and one-year MRI and Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS) assessment. At five-year follow-up, 56/62 (90.3%) completed EDSS and 40/62 additionally completed MRI (64.5%). Disability progression was defined as an increase of [≥] 1.5, [≥] 1.0 or [≥] 0.5 points for a previous EDSS score of < 1.0, 1.0 to 5.5, and [≥] 6.0, respectively. Baseline neurofilament light chain (NfL), glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), and EBNA1 immunoglobulin (IgG) titres were also measured. MTsat was calculated within normal-appearing white matter (NAWM), white matter lesions (WML), cortical and deep grey matter (GM) structures. Associations between change in MTsat and disability progression were assessed with binomial logistic regression. Interactions with interval disease activity (i.e. new/enlarging lesions [NELs]) were investigated, and comparisons were made with healthy control test-retest data (n = 11). Exploratory analyses were performed for: (prolonged) T1; baseline metrics; blood-derived markers; diffusion-weighted imaging; and, disability-associated differences in five-year microstructural MRI trajectories. Greater baseline-to-one-year decreases in NAWM and WML MTsat were associated with baseline-to-one-year disability progression (adjusted odds ratio [95% confidence interval] = 0.255 [0.078 to 0.602] and 0.261 [0.084 to 0.638]; false discovery rate [FDR]-corrected p-value = 0.015 and 0.015). NELs did not influence these associations (interaction p-values > 0.05). One-to-five-year changes in MTsat were not associated with one-to-five-year disability progression (FDR-corrected p-values > 0.05). Neither baseline nor baseline-to-one-year MTsat changes predicted future disability progression. No exploratory analyses reached FDR-corrected statistical significance. We show for the first time that progressive NAWM and WML demyelination measured with MTsat is associated with early disability progression in recently diagnosed RRMS, independent of radiological inflammatory disease activity. Neither MTsat nor T1 are associated with longer-term progression over the subsequent four years. MTsat is sensitive to disability-relevant demyelination not visible on conventional MRI, indicates a potential early window of therapeutic opportunity in the year following diagnosis, and is a promising clinically applicable disease stratifier and surrogate endpoint for therapeutic trials.

after.title: Preprint: Optimizing Lumipulse plasma pTau217/Aβ42 ratio cutpoints in an Asian cohort with high cerebrovascular disease burden
after.authors: Chong, J. R.; Yam, A. T. Y.; Toh, A.; Jiang, G.; Ito, T.; Kobayashi, C.; Dash, A.; Sachdev, P.; Chen, C. P.; Lai, M. K.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Yong Loo Lin School of Medicine, National University of Singapore
after.abstract: The generalizability of FDA-cleared Lumipulse plasma pTau217 / A{beta}42 ratio cutpoints to Asian populations remains uncertain, especially in those with high burden of concomitant cerebrovascular disease (CeVD). We evaluated pTau217, A{beta}42 and their ratio in 205 Singapore-based participants with corresponding amyloid neuroimaging. In-house cutpoints were derived using a three-range strategy targeting 95% sensitivity and specificity. Plasma pTau217/A{beta}42 ratio outperformed pTau217 alone (area under the curve, 0.951 versus 0.925; p=0.004), with comparable performance across CeVD severities. Plasma ratio cutpoints achieved 98% negative predictive value, 88% positive predictive value, and 95% accuracy, classifying 10% as intermediate-risk. Using FDA-cleared cutpoints for our cohort retained 97% sensitivity and negative predictive value but yielded lower specificity (86%), positive predictive value (77%) and accuracy (85%), with 29% classified as intermediate-risk. Our findings support the need for population-specific validation of cutpoints from FDA-cleared blood biomarkers of brain amyloid pathology.

after.title: Preprint: Tremor Morphology Toolkit: Waveform Modulation-Based Tremor Phenotyping
after.authors: Joshi, P.; Borges, Y.; Pandey, S.; Vidailhet, M.; Fung, V.; Hallett, M.; Jinnah, H. A.; Fasano, A.; Shaikh, A. G.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Case Western Reserve University
after.abstract: Clinicians typically characterize tremor by its frequency, amplitude, and body region affected. Other aspects also provide critical clues to the type of tremor and its underlying pathophysiology including tremor waveform morphology, consistency across cycles, and variability in amplitude and timing. We introduce the Tremor Morphology Toolkit (TMT), an eight metric, waveform derived panel that quantifies these features from upper limb inertial signals. Using accelerometer and gyroscope recordings from 34 individuals with upper-extremity tremor across four standardized tasks (rest, outstretched, wing beating, and kinetic), we computed: (i) rSHAPE, cycle shape consistency via pairwise similarity of normalized cycles; (ii) rSINE, sinusoidality, the mean correlation of each cycle with its best fit sinusoid; (iii) rCVA, the coefficient of variation of cycle amplitude; (iv) rCVD, the coefficient of variation of cycle duration; (v) AWI, amplitude warping index; (vi) DWI, duration warping index; (vii) FreqVar, a spectral bandwidth indexing power weighted frequency spread; and (viii) Amplitude Breathing indices, which quantify slow waxing and waning of tremor amplitude over time from fluctuations in the signal envelope, representing the time varying amplitude of the tremor waveform. We detail algorithms, parameterizations, and implementation defaults to support reproducible use. TMT is designed to complement conventional frequency amplitude measures by capturing tremor morphology and modulation in a simple, interpretable framework. It enables objective quantification of features often assessed qualitatively at the bedside, facilitates comparisons across recording conditions, and provides a foundation for validation against clinical labels and disease phenotypes. Future studies can integrate these parameters with electrophysiological measures to investigate mechanisms underlying tremor generation and modulation.

after.authors: Wendelberger, B.; Allen-Savietta, C.; Crawford, A.; Brumm, M. C.; Choi, S. H.; Kopil, C. M.; Schneider, R. B.; Kuhl, M. M.; Lafontant, D.-E.; Ecklund, D.; Fabrizio, K.; Foroud, T.; Goldstein, F. S.; Kamp, C.; Kieburtz, K.; Larson, D. N.; Luthra, N.; Pavese, N.; Siderowf, A.; Stanley, C. E.; Tanner, C. M.; Tropea, T. F.; Willson, T.; Chowdhury, S.; Marek, K.; Simuni, T.; Coffey, C. S.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Berry Consultants, LLC, Austin, Texas 78746, United States
after.abstract: The Path to Prevention (P2P) platform trial is a first-in-class, phase 2A, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled learning study. Its design expedites the assessment of investigational therapies for the treatment of early-stage Neuronal a-Synuclein Disease (NSD), a biological disease continuum that encompasses and often precedes clinically manifest Parkinson's Disease. P2P is embedded within the Parkinson's Precision Medicine Initiative (PPMI), a robust observational longitudinal cohort study on Parkinson's disease progression and a trial-facilitating enrollment framework. A regimen, comprised of an active investigational therapy and a matched placebo control, evaluates a therapeutic candidate within the P2P perpetual platform framework. Multiple regimens can be enrolled, enabling efficient testing of multiple therapeutics. A two-stage randomization scheme determines regimen sample size with 125 participants assigned to a regimen's active therapy and a variable number to placebo control. The treated follow up period is a minimum of 96 weeks and a maximum of 144 weeks, with the last randomized participant followed for 96 weeks. As a pioneering interventional trial in early-stage NSD, P2P endpoint selection was critically informed by modeling and analysis of available PPMI data. In P2P, regimens will be evaluated for efficacy using two primary endpoints: 1) a biomarker outcome of Dopamine Transporter Single-Photon Emission Computed Tomography (DAT SPECT) imaging measured by the bilateral putamen Specific Binding Ratio (SBR) and 2) a clinical outcome measured by the Movement Disorder Society-Sponsored Revision of the Unified Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale (MDS-UPDRS) Part III score. Each endpoint will be assessed separately using a longitudinal Bayesian mixed effects model, which compares the active treatment group to the shared placebo control group. The model uses regimen-specific controls at full weight and dynamically discounts controls from other regimens. Additionally, placebo control estimates are supplemented by non-randomized control data from the PPMI cohort. Clinical trial simulations, informed by longitudinal data from 275 P2P-eligible PPMI study participants (Age 60-81, 35% Female, 65% Male), were conducted to evaluate the design. Each regimen is well-powered to detect a 40% slowing in progression for both the clinical and biomarker primary endpoints when comparing active treatment to randomized control data. Supplementing the control estimation with non-randomized, P2P-eligible registry participant data increases power in the explored scenarios up to 4% for each endpoint. The embedded P2P platform trial is a powerful learning study that leverages statistical efficiencies from the platform trial design and established PPMI infrastructure and is poised to advance treatment development in early-stage NSD.

after.authors: Schneider, R. B.; Coffey, C. S.; Kopil, C. M.; Kuhl, M. M.; Allen-Savietta, C.; Brumm, M. C.; Choi, S. H.; Crawford, A.; Ecklund, D.; Fabrizio, K.; Foroud, T.; Goldstein, F. M.; Willson, T.; Chowdhury, S.; Marek, K.; Simuni, T.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Berry Consultants, LLC, Austin, Texas 78746, United States
after.abstract: The development of biologically targeted therapeutics (BTTs) that slow Parkinson's disease progression has been hampered by a reliance on testing interventions in clinically defined populations with already advanced pathobiology. Publications on the biological definition and classification of neuronal a-synuclein disease (NSD), and the development of the NSD integrated staging system (NSD-ISS), have generated a framework for identifying individuals with NSD prior to the emergence of a clinically defined syndrome. Path to Prevention (P2P) is a phase 2A, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled platform trial designed to assess the safety and efficacy of interventions in an early-stage NSD population. The trial is embedded within the observational Parkinson's Precision Medicine Initiative (PPMI), a structure that enables recruitment of participants from the PPMI cohort, leverages existing operational infrastructure, and utilizes data from non-P2P enrolled PPMI participants in the Bayesian statistical modeling. P2P will enroll participants at least 60 years of age with NSD Stage 2B (abnormal -synuclein, dopaminergic dysfunction, and prodromal signs or symptoms without functional impairment) without a clinically defined diagnosis of PD or a related disorder. As a platform trial, P2P will enable the testing of multiple interventions under a Master Protocol at approximately 35 sites across North America and Europe. Interventions are selected from industry-submitted applications based on biological relevance of the targets, and on the adequacy of the safety data appropriate to the target population. Each treatment regimen will have 125 participants on active treatment and at least 125 shared placebo control participants. Participants will remain on treatment for a maximum of 144 weeks or until 96 weeks since the randomization of the last participant. P2P has two primary endpoints, 1) rate of change in mean putamen specific binding ratio from baseline through follow-up and, 2) rate of change in the MDS-UPDRS Part III motor examination from baseline through follow-up or initiation of dopaminergic treatment. A range of secondary and exploratory biomarker-focused endpoints will be assessed. The protocol was developed with input from multiple stakeholders, including people with early-stage NSD, biopharmaceutical industry leaders, and regulatory authorities. P2P is the first trial to test biologically targeted assets in biologically defined prodromal participants utilizing an efficient platform design, which will provide the field with tools to expand therapeutic development, and enable intervention at earlier stages of neurodegeneration. P2P is scheduled to begin enrollment in December 2026 and is committed to data sharing and broad dissemination of learnings from the study.

after.authors: Pohlman, A.; Marten, A. D.; Fontes Noronha, M.; Khemmani, M.; Wolfe, A.; Abdelsattar, Z. M.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Loyola University Chicago Stritch School of Medicine
after.abstract: Background: The lung fosters a diverse microbiome that may have a complex interplay with underlying diseases, such as lung cancer. However, existing literature has revealed diverse results, likely owing to small sample sizes and diverse sampling methods. In this context, we aim to characterize the lung microbiome and its association with malignancy via multiple sampling methods during lung resection. Methods: Patients undergoing lung resection for confirmed malignancy were prospectively included in the study. During the operation, a bronchial swab and a parenchymal biopsy of lung tissue were collected from the resected specimen and sent for analysis via 16S rRNA gene amplicon (V4) sequencing. An established bioinformatics pipeline was used to determine taxonomic identification and compare these results to clinical and tumor data. Results: There were 83 participants included, with 75 (90.4%) patients having primary lung tumors and 8 (9.6%) having metastatic lesions. Resections included lobectomy (69.9%), wedge (25.3%), and segmentectomy (4.8%). Lung microbiome composition differed by primary malignancy site (lung vs metastatic; p=0.014) and tumor mutations (TP53, p=0.040; KRAS, p=0.054). For primary lung cancer, there was no difference in microbiome composition by tumor histology. A near-significant association was noted for patients with prolonged air leaks and alpha diversity of the lung microbiome (p=0.070). Conclusions: In this study, we demonstrate associations between the lung microbiome and underlying malignancy and tumor characteristics. Validation of these results may assist with diagnostic, prognostic, and therapeutic interventions in the operative and peri-operative management of lung cancer.

after.authors: Tsaggaris, J. C.; Mimouni, N.; Judy, R. L.; Xue, D.; Morley, M. P.; Wang, X.; Cotney, J. L.; Kelly, D. P.; Day, S. M.; Cappola, T. P.; Penn Medicine BioBank,  ; Damrauer, S. M.; Levin, M. G.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Division of Cardiovascular Medicine, Department of Medicine; Department of Genetics; Cardiovascular Institute, Perelman School of Medicine, University of Pennsy
after.abstract: Cardiac remodeling underlies cardiomyopathy and heart failure, yet how common genetic effects are organized across the four chambers, and whether they influence phenotypic variability beyond additive genetic effects, remains unclear. We analyzed 22 cardiac magnetic resonance phenotypes in up to 77,271 UK Biobank participants. Additive mapping identified 748 locus-trait associations across 239 regions. Multivariate fine-mapping revealed that 96% of signals showed effects across multiple cardiac chambers, while resolving independent signals with distinct anatomical profiles, including predominantly atrial and ventricular signals at RBM20. Fine-mapped signal sharing formed three robust communities corresponding broadly to atrial function, chamber remodeling and ventricular systolic function. Variance mapping identified 19 associations, 13 without a nearby additive signal. Individual variance loci and polygenic effects generalized to clinical echocardiographic phenotypes and outcomes in the Penn Medicine Biobank. These findings reveal cardiac common-variant architecture as broadly shared yet locally heterogeneous and identify phenotypic variability as a partly distinct genetic dimension.

after.authors: Esteban-Medina, A.; Loucera, C.; Dopazo, J.; Romero Gomez, M.
after.author_corresponding_institution: BarcelonaBeta Brain Research Center
after.abstract: Background: Although direct-acting antivirals have transformed hepatitis C virus (HCV) treatment, 25-30% of active infections in Spain remain undiagnosed. We aimed to develop and validate an interpretable machine-learning model to identify undiagnosed HCV infection using only data already recorded within the health system. Materials and Methods: We conducted a retrospective, population-based cohort study using the Andalusian Population Health Database (BPS). Individuals diagnosed with HCV between 2017 and 2024 (n=25,028) were matched, up to 10:1, to controls by birth year, sex, and health district. An Explainable Boosting Machine was trained on 2017-2022 data, with a threshold set in a 2023 validation set to guarantee [≥]60% sensitivity, then evaluated unmodified in an independent, non-matched, population-representative 2024 sample approximating real-world screening. Predictors comprised chronic-disease diagnoses and laboratory summary statistics recorded [≥]30 days before the index date; age and sex were excluded as matching variables. Predictors reflecting socioeconomic proxies or matching artefacts (pharmaceutical co-payment category, a zone-level deprivation index) were removed after explainability review. Results: In the independent test set, the model achieved an AUC of 0.837 (0.826 in validation), sensitivity 63.5%, specificity 91.8%, positive predictive value 7.0%, and negative predictive value 99.6%. Leading predictors were minimum alanine aminotransferase, HIV infection, dependence on non-tobacco substances, and platelet-count statistics, forming a clinically coherent, laboratory- and comorbidity-driven profile. Conclusion: An explainable model built exclusively from routine electronic health record data can identify undiagnosed HCV infection with discrimination comparable to previously published tools, evaluated under conditions approximating true population prevalence. Bias-auditing was feasible without sacrificing interpretability, supporting a scalable, equity-conscious instrument for the final phase of HCV elimination.

after.authors: Guang, H.; Zhang, Z.; Qu, J.; Ma, J.; Wu, J.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Inner Mongolia University
after.abstract: Typing dynamics are being investigated as a digital behavioral marker for Parkinson's disease (PD), but the cross-dataset reliability of typing-based classi ers remains uncertain. We evaluated four public datasets (475 par ticipants; 270 with PD and 205 controls) across 12 transfer directions using split conformal prediction targeting 90% marginal coverage. In all three pri mary directions, coverage was below the 0.90 target and the one-sided tests remained signi cant after Holm correction: 0.598 (95% CI, 0.4830.704) for Tappy[->]MIT, 0.850 (0.7880.899) for MIT[->]Tappy, and 0.732 (0.6840.777) for clinical[->]self-reported transfer. Discrimination and coverage did not con sistently change together: LightGBM had lower AUC than logistic regression in all 12 directions but higher coverage in 11, with larger prediction sets. Class-conditional coverage varied by target cohort: PD-conditional cover age was 0.214 for Tappy[->]MIT, whereas healthy-control coverage was 0.700 for MIT[->]Tappy and 0.627 for clinical[->]self-reported transfer. Recalibration with 9 and 18 labeled target participants raised the lower condence bound above 0.80 in the latter two directions; in Tappy[->]MIT, it remained below 0.80 even with 25 labels. Weighted conformal prediction yielded coverage of 0.9181.000 without target labels but returned the full label set for 86% 100% of participants. Stress tests did not reproduce the observed coverage patterns, and black-box shift estimation did not support pure label shift as the dominant explanation for Tappy[->]MIT. Evaluating typing dynamics as a digital marker for PD requires cross-dataset assessment of discrimination, marginal and class-conditional coverage, and recovery costs. Clinical screen ing utility has not been established.

after.abstract: Objectives Persistent methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA) bacteraemia is associated with significant morbidity and mortality. Cefazolin-ertapenem combination therapy has demonstrated synergistic activity in preclinical models and small case series, but comparative clinical evidence is lacking. Methods We conducted a multicentre retrospective review of all patients aged >18 years with persistent MSSA bacteraemia at two Queensland tertiary hospitals between January 2014 and December 2024. The primary outcome was time to blood culture sterilisation, compared between patients who commenced cefazolin-ertapenem combination therapy prior to first negative blood culture and a matched cohort of non-combination-treated patients. Secondary outcomes included 90-day all-cause mortality, 90-day relapse, development of multi-resistant organisms, Clostridioides difficile infection, and adverse drug events. Results A total of 288 episodes of persistent MSSA bacteraemia in 283 patients were identified. Twenty-six patients received cefazolin-ertapenem combination therapy. Among the 14 patients who commenced combination therapy prior to first negative blood culture, median time to sterilisation was 1 day (IQR 1 - 2), compared with 2 days (IQR 1 - 3) in the matched non-combination group. Cox regression in the matched cohort (n=114) demonstrated an increased rate of blood culture clearance with combination therapy (HR 1.8; 95% CI 1.2 - 2.7; P =0.004). In the full cohort, ninety-day mortality (20.0% vs 23.0%, P=0.73) and relapse rates (11.5% vs 8.3%, P =0.57) did not differ significantly between groups. Conclusions Cefazolin-ertapenem combination therapy was associated with accelerated blood culture sterilisation in persistent MSSA bacteraemia. Prospective randomised evaluation is warranted.

after.authors: Nishan, R. K.; Alam, M. S.; Azad, A. K.; Sarkar, M. M. H.; Nodee, T. A.; Mia, M. Z.; Miah, M. I.; Islam, M. S.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Department of Microbiology, Jagannath University, Dhaka, Bangladesh
after.abstract: Background: Early diagnostic triage for suspected dengue is important in high-volume settings, yet confirmatory testing may be delayed or intermittently available. This study aimed to develop and internally validate a simple complete blood count (CBC)-derived score to estimate the likelihood of same-day dengue non-structural protein 1 (NS1) antigen positivity among suspected dengue patients in Dhaka, Bangladesh. Methods: We conducted a retrospective model-development study at Uttara Adhunik Medical College Hospital using data from patients with clinical suspicion of dengue between 19 August and 12 October 2023. The final analysis included 596 unique patients who underwent CBC and NS1 testing on the same day. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) penalized logistic regression was used for variable selection among routinely available demographic and hematological predictors. Selected predictors were refit using unpenalized logistic regression to derive a CBC score. Internal validation and calibration were assessed using bootstrap optimism correction with 400 resamples. Results: Among 596 patients, 306 (51.3%) were NS1 positive. The final parsimonious model retained platelet count rescaled per 10 x 109/L, white blood cell count, and monocyte count. The optimism-corrected AUC was 0.9429. At the Youden-derived cutoff of 11.825, the final integer score had sensitivity 0.833 (95% CI, 0.787-0.873), specificity 0.966 (95% CI, 0.938-0.983), PPV 0.962 (95% CI, 0.932-0.982), NPV 0.846 (95% CI, 0.802-0.883), and accuracy 0.898 (95% CI, 0.870-0.921). A rounded cutoff of 12 produced similar performance. In benchmark analysis, the final model showed a modest improvement over platelet count alone (AUC 0.944 vs 0.931; Delta AUC 0.012; DeLong p=0.00364). Conclusion: A three-parameter CBC score can estimate the likelihood of NS1 antigen positivity among suspected dengue patients in this single-center dataset. The score should be interpreted as a CBC-only triage adjunct, not as a replacement for confirmatory dengue testing. External validation in independent cohorts is needed before routine clinical use.

after.abstract: The apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) remains the standard metric for assessing obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) severity, although it does not fully capture the physiological consequences of respiratory events. Hypoxic burden (HB), which integrates the frequency, depth, and duration of oxygen desaturations, has been proposed as a more comprehensive measure of OSA-related hypoxic stress. This study compared the prognostic value of HB and AHI for subjective and objective treatment outcomes in patients undergoing continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) therapy. Data from 412 patients with OSA who underwent diagnostic and CPAP-treated polysomnography were analyzed, including 52 patients with available follow-up questionnaires. HB was calculated using a validated event-based algorithm. While AHI primarily reflects sleep fragmentation and physiological response to CPAP, HB appears more closely related to subjective treatment benefit. Incorporating HB alongside AHI may improve clinical phenotyping and prediction of treatment response in OSA.

after.title: Preprint: Biomarker-Informed Phenotyping of the Heart Failure Continuum: A Population-Based Evaluation of the Second Universal Definition of Heart Failure
after.authors: Chen, H.; Ye, J.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Cornell University
after.abstract: Objective: To develop and evaluate a biomarker-informed, computable phenotype of the heart failure (HF) continuum, aligned with 2026 AHA/ACC/ESC/WHF Expert Consensus, using NHANES and linked mortality data, and to determine whether this phenotype identifies subgroups with distinct mortality risks. Methods: We analyzed 11,477 U.S. adults aged [≥]20 years from the 1999-2004 NHANES cycles who participated in the surplus-sera biomarker substudy and were linked to National Death Index follow-up. Participants were classified into four phenotypes according to the 2026 Universal Definition of Heart Failure: no apparent risk, Stage A (at risk), Stage B (elevated NT-proBNP without self-reported HF), and Stage C (self-reported HF). Survey-weighted Kaplan-Meier curves and nested, multiply imputed Cox proportional hazards models, with sequential adjustment for demographic, socioeconomic, and cardiometabolic covariates, were used to estimate associations with mortality. Pairwise phenotype comparisons, standardized adjusted survival estimates, and restricted mean survival times were also calculated. Incremental prognostic value was evaluated by comparing discrimination and reclassification metrics between the full phenotype and a conventional three-level model that excluded NT-proBNP. Results: Weighted prevalences were 16.9%, 70.0%, 10.7%, and 2.4% for no apparent risk, Stage A, Stage B, and Stage C, respectively. In fully adjusted models, the hazard ratios (HRs) relative to no apparent risk were 1.58 (95% CI, 1.08-2.30), 2.88 (95% CI, 2.00-4.16), and 2.56 (95% CI, 1.61-4.09), respectively. Stage B was associated with significantly higher mortality risk than Stage A (HR, 1.83; 95% CI, 1.62-2.07), whereas the difference between Stage C and Stage B was not statistically significant (HR, 0.89; 95% CI, 0.71-1.11). The association for Stage B attenuated less across sequentially adjusted models than that for Stage C. Adjusted 10-year mortality risks were 15.2% for Stage B and 14.2% for Stage C. Incorporating Stage B into the conventional model yielded only marginal improvements in discrimination ({Delta}C-statistic, 0.002; 95% CI, 0.001-0.002). Conclusion: A biomarker-informed phenotype of the HF continuum can be operationalized using national survey data and identifies a pre-HF subgroup with an adjusted mortality risk not significantly different from that of individuals with overt HF, despite only marginal gains in prognostic discrimination.

after.title: Preprint: Lesion sterilisation and tissue repair with chloramphenicol, tetracycline, zinc oxide-eugenol paste compared to zinc oxide-eugenol pulpectomy in primary molars: Two-year follow-up findings of a multicentre non-inferiority randomised clinical trial
after.authors: Santos, P. S.; Ramos, T.; Fernandes, G. d. C.; Oliveira, N. M.; Rocha, A. O.; Vitali, F. C.; Galdino, F. F.; Marques, R. P. S.; Soviero, V. L. V. M.; Santana, C. M.; Fidalgo, T. K. d. S.; Cardoso, M.; Mendes, F. M.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Department of Pediatric Dentistry, School of Dentistry, Universidade de Sao Paulo (USP), Sao Paulo, Brazil
after.abstract: Background: Chloramphenicol, tetracycline, zinc oxide (CTZ) paste has been widely used, particularly in Latin America, in Lesion Sterilization and Tissue Repair (LSTR) procedures in primary molars. However, reports on its long-term efficacy are scarce. Aim: This multicentre non-inferiority randomised trial compared the efficacy of LSTR using CTZ paste with conventional zinc oxide-eugenol (ZOE) pulpectomy in primary molars. Design: 199 primary molars from children aged 3 to 9 years were randomised to the CTZ or ZOE groups. The primary outcome was clinical and radiographic success at 24 months. Clinical time, children's behaviour, immediate discomfort and postoperative pain were also evaluated. The main analysis followed the intention-to-treat (ITT) principle, comparing success proportions with the Miettinen-Nurminen method, considering a prespecified non-inferiority margin of 15% (p < 0.05). Results: Overall success rates in the ITT population were 64.3% for CTZ and 58.7% for ZOE, with a difference of 5.6% (95% CI: -9.3 to 20.4; p<0.01). Mean; standard deviation clinical time was significantly shorter in CTZ (36.3; 9.8 min) than in ZOE (63.0; 16.3 min) (p<0.01). Children's behaviour, immediate discomfort and postoperative pain were similar between groups (p>0.05). Conclusion: LSTR with CTZ paste was non-inferior to conventional ZOE pulpectomy after 24 months of follow-up.

after.authors: Simpson, V. E.; Thomas, N. J. M.; Hill, A. V.; Knupp, J.; McDonald, T. J.; Patel, K. A.; Murray Leech, J. A.; Shields, B. M.; Pearson, E. R.; Jones, A. G.
after.author_corresponding_institution: University of Exeter
after.abstract: Objective: Early progression to insulin following initial management as type 2 diabetes may indicate missed type 1 diabetes. Recent guidelines advise islet-autoantibody testing in all adults who progress to insulin within 3 years, though this has not been directly tested. We aimed to determine whether positive islet autoantibodies in this setting confirm the genetic characteristics and C-peptide progression of classical type 1 diabetes. Research Design and Methods: We compared genetic susceptibility to type 1 and type 2 diabetes (T1DGRS and T2DGRS) and prospectively assessed C-peptide loss over 3 years after diagnosis among islet-autoantibody-positive adults initially treated as having type 2 diabetes (without insulin) who progressed to insulin within 3 years (n=86), versus participants with classical type 1 (n=499) and type 2 (n=603) diabetes. Results were replicated in cross-sectional data from the DARE/GoDARTS studies (n=9466). Results: Participants who progressed to insulin within 3 years and had positive islet autoantibodies had the genetic characteristics and C-peptide loss of classical type 1 diabetes: T1DGRS -0.04 (-0.27, 0.18) vs 0.00 (-0.09, 0.09) [p=0.71], T2DGRS -0.35 (-0.59, -0.11) vs -0.35 (-0.44, -0.26) [p=0.99] and annual change in urine C-peptide creatinine ratio -47% (-55%, -40%) vs -49% (-52%, -46%) [p=0.6] respectively. In contrast, autoantibody-positive participants without early insulin (n=51) had genetic and C-peptide characteristics consistent with type 2 diabetes. Findings were similar in cross-sectional cohorts. Conclusion: Islet-autoantibody-positive individuals with early insulin requirement following initial treatment as type 2 diabetes have similar genotype and progression to classical type 1 diabetes. This supports recent guidance that they should be diagnosed and treated as type 1 diabetes.

after.authors: Brittain, J.-S.; Mills, C.; Judge, C.; Bastos, L. S.; Freitas, L. P.; Carvalho, L. M.; Araujo, E. C.; Coelho, F. C.; Xu, Y.; Reddy, B.; Pasumarthi, R. K.; Shekel, T.; Shetty, S.; Chou, A. C.-Y.; Carter, A.; Muslim, A.; Prasad, G.; Widner, K.; Bharel, M.; Scarpino, S. V.; Flaxman, S.; Bhatt, S.; Tsui, J. L. H.; Kraemer, M. U. G.
after.author_corresponding_institution: University of Oxford
after.abstract: Accurate and timely probabilistic dengue forecasts can support public health preparedness, but producing reliable forecasts across locations and time horizons remains challenging. We evaluated five statistical, machine-learning, deep-learning, and foundation-model approaches for forecasting monthly reported dengue cases across 5,570 Brazilian municipalities at 1-, 3-, 6- and 12-month horizons, with forecasts backtested from January 2020 to August 2025. The time-series foundation model TimesFM maintained comparatively stable probabilistic forecast performance at longer horizons, while most other models showed declining performance. We then tested whether spatial representations of human and environmental context from a Population Dynamics Foundation Model (PDFM) could improve forecasts through post-hoc residual adjustment. PDFM adjustment improved mean probabilistic forecast performance, measured by the Weighted Interval Score (WIS), in 19 of 20 model-horizon combinations, although the magnitude and frequency of improvements varied across models, horizons and municipalities. The largest improvements were observed for N-BEATS, including a reduction in mean WIS of 1.13 at the six-month horizon (95% CI [0.84, 1.48]; Diebold-Mariano p < 0.0001), with improvements also observed for XGBoost. The proportion of forecasts improved by PDFM generally increased with locally reported dengue case counts, although this relationship varied between models. Covariate selection, spatial fitting and forecast aggregation strategies showed strong model-dependent effects, while monthly model retraining provided no consistent advantage in the settings evaluated. Together, these findings highlight the potential of pretrained representations for dengue forecasting, with benefits dependent on forecasting architecture, horizon and modelling configuration.
